correctness.rationale: The 1D circle can be cut at an uncovered point, unless footprints partition the entire circle; ordered equal-length intervals then show every multiplicity >=2 point lies in the middle arc, so m2+m3<=ell. The success probability is an exact affine function of multiplicity lengths constrained by a sharp triangle whose three vertices are geometrically attainable. Comparing them gives the exact maximum, necessary-and-sufficient regimes and the two equality boundaries; symbolic algebra validates the threshold differences. An independent endpoint-partition checker passed 18,000 random continuous samples plus 14 boundary checks. Finite sampling is supplementary to the proof.

value.rationale: Seismic early-warning protocols face an established scientific tradeoff between acting on one receiver and requiring network confirmation. The result identifies the smallest receiver count with a genuinely intermediate redundancy optimum, constructs three spatially separate stations achieving it, and establishes a complete sharp phase diagram and equality cases independent of footprint size under a motivated sparse limit. The result is an analytic design benchmark and is not claimed to be a measured real-world policy; the precise mixed-alarm payoff and station-layout optimization are motivated by source literature, not arbitrary numerical slicing.
